In my experience throughput is much lower on Box. Also there's no desktop client for Linux.
Max file size is 250 megabyte on Box's free tier, unlike Dropbox which does not have any limits.
The user interface is not as intuitive as Dropbox's. Box, at least on the Mac, doesn't integrate as nicely as Dropbox. The web interface is very unintuitive and overstuffed with features.

The Box client used to spike CPU at 100% on OS X when you have a folder hierarchy with a lot of small files, because it enumerated folders/files instead of hooking into OS X file system notifications.
There's only 10GB of bandwidth for the month on Box's free tier - you'd need 5 months just to upload to your max storage.
Signed up, the desktop client seems a lot clunkier than Dropbox (Windows 7). Dropbox somewhat perfected the model; the 'Default Sync Folder' concept in Box is a real bummer.
No luck on the Linux front for Box, although they seem to offer WebDAV access — a far cry from a syncing solution such as Dropbox or AeroFS.
I use Box alongside Dropbox and Google Drive and as far as I can tell it's as good as either of those.
We really liked Box for the corporate account since it's possible to selectively grant outside parties access to files/folders.
It keeps out all the free and essentially unaccountable users who would like to use Box for movie/software/game piracy, likely explaining the file size limits on free accounts.
